A-window refix round 2. Before continuing, I checked what the stopped refixer had left in HEAD. All four of the verifier's minor items are done and correct in code:
- The S72 note now cites D046, not D043.
- `.mxrHelp` adds no empty tooltip for network media.
- The PiP placeholder icon uses `MXRPlayerMetrics.pictureInPictureIcon` (the 24 pt `Theme.Metric.iconSize` × 2), no longer the play button's width.
- The A-08 toast is rewritten with ViewThatFits. At 640 pt with the compact library it drops the message and keeps only Continue Watching and close; no more "You alr…". I checked the narrow and wide renders by eye.

The Player-6 gate cause (cross-item 2) was the media fixture. It had 2 queue items with the current one last, so Next was disabled and dimmed, while Player-6 shows Next enabled. The refixer changed it to 3 items. `testShippingWindowMatchesFigmaPlayer6OutsideDocumentedDeviations` now returns PASS in all four regions, and a crop of the transport region matches Figma by eye.

F-06 (cross-item 1) is new in this round: a documented per-entry deviation mechanism for the snapshot tool.
- `GalleryEntry.figmaDeviations: [FigmaDeviation]` declares two kinds, each with a decision id and a reason:
  - `.removed(figmaNode, gap:, decision:)` cuts that Figma row or section band out of the reference. The rows below it shift up and are still compared pixel for pixel at their product position. Only the strip the cut uncovers at the bottom of the column is skipped.
  - `.differs(rect, decision:)` leaves out a rect where the product intentionally draws something else, for example a different default value.
- `FigmaIndex.applying(_:render:reference:)` applies them, cutting bottom-up and checking that each node descends from the entry's frame. No thresholds were changed.
- `mxr-snapshot check` applies the deviations, lists them in the report with the share of the canvas not compared, and takes `--ignore-deviations` for raw output.
- The declarations live in a new file, SettingsFigmaDeviations.swift. Rows removed under D035 are declared in general, general-advanced, interface, privacy, controls, playback, library, network, performance and recording. Product defaults that differ from Figma are declared too: D035 dialogs ON, D030 Continue "Ask", D030 Play locally OFF.

S48 results at 2× after declaring:
- PASS or REVIEW: general, playback, privacy, video, subtitles, controls, library, network, recording.
- Still FAIL on differences no decision covers: interface, general-advanced, audio, performance, extensions. These are listed in the gate test with XCTExpectFailure (non-strict) and reported below.

New tests: FigmaDeviationTests (4) and ContinueWatchingToastTests (2). These targeted suites pass: WindowCompositionTests 12, GalleryRenderTests 13, AnchoredPopupPinPolicyTests 3, PlayerProgressRegressionTests 4, OSDLayoutTests 2. My files build with no new warnings.

reports.summary:
A-window refix round 3. I fixed the verifier's major finding and its anchoring minor. The third item belongs to the library owner and is passed on below.

**Major: the Settings gate depended on test order.** I found the root cause by experiment. The `AppleFontSmoothing` setting is read once per process, the first time AppKit is touched: `NSApplication.shared`, any `NSFont`, or measuring a hosting view. A setting made after that changes nothing. Pre-check reruns:
- the pair `ContinueWatchingToastTests|FigmaDeviationTests` failed every time;
- `DialogsTests|PanelsTests|<gate>` failed too, so any earlier test that touches AppKit triggers it, not only the toast test.

I tried two ways to apply the setting before every test and dropped both:
- An early hook in the test bundle. Overriding `defaultTestSuite` makes filtered XCTest runs silently drop the class, which I checked in a scratch package.
- Turning smoothing off on the drawing context. SwiftUI text ignores it.

The gate now runs each S48 Settings check in its own `mxr-snapshot check --id … --scale 2` process, four at a time. The CLI applies the setting first thing in main, so the gate's verdict is exactly what the CLI reports. The run time dropped from about 40 s to about 18 s.

**Recording.** Its verdict is now a steady REVIEW (1532 px, the CLI figure). Its differences have no covering decision:
- '~/Movies' where Figma shows '~/Videos';
- 'Default (Medium)' where Figma shows 'Medium';
- ⓘ icons on Include video and Include subtitles.

So I listed recording in `openSettingsDifferences` with that reason, as the verifier allowed.

**Minor: hard-coded `differs` y positions.** I added `FigmaDeviation.differs(node:outset:)` (kind `.differsAt`). The area left out is the box of a Figma node, moved up by every removed band above it in its column. The general, general-advanced, playback and recording value deviations now point at the Figma Toggle or Dropdown node instead of a rect worked out by hand. They are tighter, too: the playback area is now 320×36 instead of 320×46. The citation check also covers anchored nodes. A new test, `testNodeAnchoredDifferenceFollowsRemovedRows`, checks two things in Recording:
- the area left out is at the product's toggle position, 147 pt above Figma's (the removed Casting section);
- the row now drawn at Figma's position is still compared.

I did not edit DECISIONS.md for the D030 product-default citations. That is the owner's and orchestrator's call; see ownerDecisions.

Results:
- Pair `ContinueWatchingToastTests|FigmaDeviationTests`: passes twice in a row.
- `ContinueWatchingToastTests|DialogsTests|FigmaDeviationTests`: passes, with DialogsTests touching AppKit first.
- The full targeted set (WindowComposition, AnchoredPopupPinPolicy, PlayerProgressRegression, GalleryRender, OSDLayout, ContinueWatchingToast, FigmaDeviation): 41 tests, 0 failures.
- GalleryRenderTests and WindowCompositionTests also pass when DialogsTests and PanelsTests run before them, so only the Settings gate was order-sensitive.
- `swift build`: clean.
fixed: Major (gate order dependence): the cause is that the font-smoothing setting is read once per process, the first time AppKit is touched, so any earlier test that touches AppKit made recording FAIL. testSettingsCategoriesMatchFigmaOutsideDocumentedDeviations now runs each S48 Settings check in its own mxr-snapshot process (4 in parallel), so it gives the same verdict as the CLI in any order. Checked: the pair passes twice in a row, the run with DialogsTests first passes, and the targeted set is 41/41.

Major (b) recording: its undocumented differences are listed in openSettingsDifferences with the exact reason: ~/Movies, Default (Medium), and the ⓘ on Include video and Include subtitles. Its verdict is now a steady REVIEW, 1532 px, the same as the CLI.

The general, general-advanced, playback and recording deviations now point at the Toggle or Dropdown node: 3046:9900, 3046:9356, 3062:12858 and 6571:16804. New test testNodeAnchoredDifferenceFollowsRemovedRows; the citation and ancestry test also covers anchored nodes.

verdict.summary:
A-window round 3 holds up: no blocker or major issue that code, tests or renders can establish. The only remaining part is the real-window check for A-05, which goes to liveChecks.

**Build and tests**
- `swift build --build-tests` is clean.
- Order test: I ran `ContinueWatchingToastTests`, `DialogsTests`, `FigmaDeviationTests` and `PanelsTests` together. `DialogsTests` touches AppKit before the gate runs, and all 32 tests passed. The Settings gate no longer depends on test order, because each check runs in its own mxr-snapshot process.
- Targeted set: `WindowCompositionTests` (12), `AnchoredPopupPinPolicyTests` (3), `PlayerProgressRegressionTests` (4), `GalleryRenderTests` (13) and `OSDLayoutTests` (2). All 34 passed.
- Logs are in `<scratch>`.

**Cross-area items**
- **(1) F-06 deviation mechanism.** `FigmaDeviation` supports three kinds of deviation:
  - `removed`: a Figma row the product leaves out; it is cut from the reference and the rows below are still compared.
  - `differs`: a rect where the product draws something else.
  - `differsAt`: the same, anchored to a Figma node and moved up by the rows removed above it.
  
  Every deviation must cite an accepted decision, and a test checks that each one does and that each anchored node belongs to the entry's Figma frame. Another test draws a wrong block outside every declared area and confirms the check still FAILs. There is no global threshold change. The edit to SettingsGallery.swift is minimal.
  
  My CLI runs gave these verdicts:
  - recording: REVIEW
  - playback: REVIEW
  - general: REVIEW
  - general-advanced: FAIL. This is a real open difference: I looked at the side-by-side, and Show minor warnings and Additional command line options are missing.
  - performance: FAIL, listed as open with its reason.
- **(2) Player-6 transport region.** The strict test now gets a PASS for "transport and elapsed time" and the other three regions. The whole-entry check still reports FAIL at the playhead (346,1040). That is the documented position difference: Figma's own times put the playhead at 8.4 %.
- **(3) A-08 resume toast.** I rendered S12.Window/continue-narrow and looked at it. The toast now shows only Continue Watching and close, sits in the middle of the visible video to the right of the compact library, and nothing is truncated. A test measures the toast's real fitted size at the narrow and wide widths.

**Earlier minor issues are fixed**
- The title tooltip uses `mxrHelp(optional)`, so non-file media no longer get an empty tooltip.
- The PiP icon has its own metric, `MXRPlayerMetrics.pictureInPictureIcon`.
- The S72 note now cites D046 instead of the superseded D043.

**Hard rules**
- No engine edits: `git diff upstream-base-2026-10-14 -- src lib include modules/gui/macosx` is empty.
- No literal design values were added.
- No masks or thresholds hide differences.
